agent_responses.reasoning: After reading both artifacts, I am recommending a BLOCK at the design gate. There are two blocking-severity issues: (1) full card numbers are logged in plaintext to CloudWatch with no redaction — a direct PII and likely PCI violation baked into the design — and (2) there is no PCI-DSS scope review documented anywhere for a service that explicitly processes card numbers. These alone justify blocking. Additionally, there are four high/medium concerns: no log retention policy, no business-level success metric (only infra SLOs), no rollback plan, and no cost ceiling on autoscaling. The team should resolve the two blocking issues and address the high-severity gaps before resubmitting to this gate.

agent_responses.reasoning: This design presents two blocking concerns that prevent gate approval. First, full card numbers (PANs) and customer names are logged in plaintext to CloudWatch — this simultaneously violates PCI DSS (which prohibits unmasked PAN storage in logs) and constitutes unredacted PII under GDPR/CCPA. Second, there is a complete absence of a PCI scope assessment despite the service directly processing card transaction data. Beyond these blockers, the design omits a CloudWatch log retention policy (compounding the PII and cost risk), provides no autoscaling cost ceiling for a 5,000 RPS service, and contains no cost estimate at all. Vendor SLAs for CloudWatch are unacknowledged, and cross-region egress costs are unmodeled. The project must at minimum: (1) implement PAN/PII redaction before any log write, (2) commission a PCI scope/CDE boundary assessment, (3) set a CloudWatch log retention policy, (4) define an autoscaling cap and provide a cost estimate before returning to this gate.
